title: candidate-feedback-draft-nina-park-2026-03-11
content:
Notes to self / scratchpad for hiring discussion:

Candidate: Nina Park — Senior Applied ML Engineer (on-site loop 2026-03-11)
Interviewer panel: Priya (applied-ml), Alicia (serving-runtime), Daniel (owner)

Quick summary:
- Strong systems-first ML background (latency-focused optimizations, experience with dynamic batching)
- Interview felt practical: good intuition for KV cache, batching tradeoffs, memory/CPU/GPU balance
- Some gaps in probabilistic reasoning (uncertainty calibration) and evaluation metrics for ranking tasks

Strengths:
- Clear mental model for inference pipeline: batching, cache invalidation, warm-starting models
- Has production experience shipping quantized models (INT8) and debugging perf regressions on GPUs
- Communicates tradeoffs succinctly; good at prioritizing engineering cost vs. quality

Weaknesses / Risks:
- Limited exposure to large-scale AB testing and rollout frameworks (A/B, canary) — asked about rollout strategy, answer was basic
- Uncomfortable with some statistical evals: struggled with defining appropriate null hypothesis for reranking test
- Mostly infra+engineering focus; may need ramp on designing eval suites/tiered metrics for quality monitoring

Coding exercise (45m live):
- Implemented simplified streaming tokenizer + batching wrapper in Python.
- Code was readable, used correct concurrency primitives (asyncio) but missed one edge-case around cancellation and cleanup.
- With probing questions, candidate fixed bug quickly.

System design (60m):
- Designed an architecture for a multi-tenant inference endpoint with latency SLOs. Good decomposition: ingress -> routing -> batching -> model pool -> cache -> metrics.
- Suggested sensible fallback policies (smaller model variant), but lacked concrete autoscaling thresholds and backpressure mechanisms (we sketched them together).

Behavior / team fit:
- Collaborative, asks clarifying Qs, receptive to feedback.
- Feels like a good IC; likely to pair well with runtime/infra teams.

Open questions to resolve before panel decision:
- How deep is their familiarity with config-driven rollouts and feature flags in prod? (ask Priya to follow up with example from their last role)
- Compensation expectations and notice period (have HR confirm)
- Can they present a short post-hire plan for first 90 days focused on improving inference throughput/costs?

Suggested next steps:
- Move to hiring committee / panel review; recommend a follow-up focused on evaluation metrics and AB testing experience (30m) — Priya to take lead.
- If committee likes, propose leveling to Senior (IC4) with strong IC path; note some ramp on evaluation tooling expected.

Recommendation (tentative): "Strong Consider" — hire if panel checks AB testing/eval experience in follow-up.

Misc notes / links:
- Candidate slide deck shared in recruiting PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/recruiting/pull/98
- Referenced paper on KV caching (candidate mentioned): https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.00001 (note: follow up to get exact ref)
- Slack thread: #hiring-panel — see comments from Alicia about cancellation bug reproduction

TODO (personal):
- Draft feedback email template (neutral + highlights) in case we decide not to move forward
- Add anonymized summary to hiring dashboard with rubric scores (accuracy: 3/5, systems: 5/5, coding: 4/5, culture: 4/5)

-- Daniel
